methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Innoviz Technologies (INVZ) operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector as a recently public company. The valuation universe for this stage and sector is constrained: while seven private competitors exist in Drones & Autonomous—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—no public comparables are available. This absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage public peers with sufficient scale creates a narrow foundation for traditional peer-based triangulation.

The peer-median approach is not applicable to this analysis. The sector contains only seven private-stage companies, but none satisfy the minimum criteria of three same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers needed for statistically meaningful comparison. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise and misrepresent Innoviz's specific profile relative to its true competitive set.

Without sufficient public market data, a full triangulation is not supportable from the available information. A robust valuation would require additional methods—such as discounted cash flow analysis using Innoviz-specific unit economics, precedent transaction analysis from Drones & Autonomous M&A activity, or expansion of the comparable set to include adjacent autonomy subsectors with public representation. The current data constraints prevent quantitative synthesis into a defensible valuation range. Future analysis should prioritize either narrowing to a tighter peer subset with comparable financials or employing intrinsic valuation methods independent of market comparables.
